question: A 59-year-old presents with right-sided hemiparesis, right-sided sensory loss, leftward eye deviation, and slurred speech. A head CT is performed which is significant for a hyperdense lesion affecting the putamen. The patient has a history of hypertension treated with hydrochlorothiazide, but is non-adherent. Which of the following is most likely associated with the cause of this patient’s neurological deficits?

options.opa: Thrombotic development over ruptured atherosclerotic plaque
options.opc: Amyloid deposition in small cortical vessels
options.opd: Predisposed vessel rupture secondary to cortical atrophy
options.ope: Saccular aneurysm rupture into the subarachnoid space
